visual_qa_labels: a black and white figure from the 1955 Cohen Inquiry report showing the Comet G-ALYU pressure-test fuselage rupture at the forward escape hatch
inside view of a de Havilland Comet fuselage failure during water tank fatigue testing, with torn skin around an open hatch
visual_qa_negative_labels: a complete modern passenger airliner flying in a blue sky
factual_notes: 1955 Court of Inquiry report: G-ALYU burst after 3,057 pressure cycles (1,221 actual and 1,836 simulated), with the test rupture at the forward escape hatch (Fig. 7; pp. 24-27). The in-service G-ALYP crack origin was a rivet hole at the rear ADF window cut-out. https://asn.flightsafety.org/reports/1954/19540408_COMT_G-ALYY.pdf

factual_notes: 1955 Court of Inquiry report: fatigue crack growth initiated at a rivet hole at the rear ADF window cut-out.
